Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 1228 PM EST Tue Nov 3 2026

- Mild and breezy today with near record high temperatures and gusty
  winds up to 30 mph. 

- Mild conditions continue Wednesday with light rain likely.

&&

.AVIATION...

Low pressure and connecting cold fronts stretch from northern 
Ontario to the Gulf coast, roughly along the MS valley this 
afternoon. An equally broad warm sector also extends from the SE 
States into the Great Lakes which has broken mid level VFR clouds 
established across southern Lower Mi. Recent satellite trends 
indicate decreasing coverage of the mid cloud layer as it tracks NE, 
replaced by a scattered daytime heating component. 

S-SW wind gusting near 30 kts is also a result of maximum boundary 
layer mixing through peak heating this afternoon. The gust component 
lingers less frequently after sunset within a neutral boundary layer 
thermal profile which then stabilizes toward midnight. There is some 
LLWS indicated in model soundings but not quite to the intensity for 
a mention in the forecast. The aviation weather highlight shifts to 
the moisture axis and bands of showers moving in from the Midwest 
and also developing northward from the Ohio valley late tonight and 
Wednesday morning. This brings a lengthy period of mixed MVFR/IFR 
ceiling and mostly MVFR visibility until the cold front sweeps 
through late Wednesday. 

For DTW... Wind gusting near 30 kts this afternoon holds from the SW 
direction while diminishing this evening. Coverage of VFR ceiling 
above 5000 ft is also on the decrease this afternoon setting up 
scattered sky condition this evening. Clouds quickly increase and 
drop below 5000 ft again after midnight trending down to MVFR by 
sunrise and then IFR during Wednesday morning. 

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* High for ceiling 5000 ft or less late tonight and Wednesday.
